_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution: the mutation vocabulary belongs to ONE subset of ONE standard of ONE artifact, so its oracle registration and catalog live here rather than in a shared manifest. `stdio.semio.model` is a semio-NATIVE format — no third party reads or writes `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` for it — so the reference registered below is a second IMPLEMENTATION in another language rather than a third-party package.

oracles.rationale:
No library in any ecosystem reads or writes semio's own `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope. IfcOpenShell and ruststep were surveyed again and are still not oracles for THIS vocabulary: they read IFC and STEP, they can only reach a `SemioModelSnapshot` through this repository's own import/export bridge — which would make the comparison run our importer against our exporter — and neither can express `set-snapshot` at all. The second producer is therefore a second IMPLEMENTATION: `../../../../../../🧪️tests/mutate-semio-model/🐍️component.py`, which carries the semio envelope, the `stdio.semio.model` DSL grammar with its spatial-kind/element-class/geometry-ref/pset-value/relation-kind vocabularies, the LEB128 pack frame with its little-endian `f64` transforms, and all fourteen verbs with their inverses, written in Python from the committed specification documents alone — `../🚪️io/📝️text/📸️snapshot/📖️.grammar.semio`, `../🚪️io/💾️binary/📸️snapshot/📡️.protocol.semio`, `../🚪️io/📝️text/🧬️mutations/📖️.grammar.semio`, the committed `(before, mutation, after)` vectors in the case's own `🧫️fixtures/`, and the envelope region of `🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🧬️semio/🦀️.rs`. It imports nothing from and transliterates nothing of the Rust it judges, and it needs no host package, which is why `package` is empty. The protocol description stops at the repeated `spatial`/`elements`/`relations` records and names only their shape; that shape was turned into a reader and a writer by taking the field order from the DSL grammar and every enum ordinal from the order that grammar declares its alternatives in, and the derivation is PINNED by the implementation re-encoding the committed `../../✉️base/📚️examples/🏢️building/🖼️assets/🎒️.pack.semio` byte for byte. IfcOpenShell 0.8.4 IS used, but for what it is authoritative about: reading the real committed Nakagin Capsule Tower IFC 4 model once, to derive the 3-spatial-node, 181-element, 362-relation artifact the case mutates.

UNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `semio-v1-model-mutate`'s external-oracle requirement for its 11-kind mutation vocabulary; a qualifying third-party reference (`third-party-library` / `third-party-cli` / `standards-reference-tool`) is still owed.

[2026-09-02, D1 — SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION] Promoted from cross-semio-implementation to verified-native-second-implementation: this artifact is semio-native (isSemioNativeArtifact), this reference's own third-party survey above (kept verbatim) already names what was checked and declined, its python implementation differs from the Rust subject, and it covers 100% of this manifest's 1 capability/capabilities with 1 committed fixture vector(s). See .🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION/📓️d1-native-oracle-discharge.md.
